text: Upgrade zod from v3 to v4 across the packages (audit high: oversized constrained collections)
description: pnpm audit --prod (2026-11-09) reports zod <4.6.6 'can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections' (high). Used by backend, mcp, shared, agent-tools, loop-worker, real-world (^3.24-3.25). No v3 fix is listed. Mitigated meanwhile by the 8 MiB request cap (ed16c952). Risks of the upgrade: v4 changes z.string().uuid() to strict RFC 9562 (z.guid() is the loose form), so ids or fixtures that are UUID-shaped but not RFC-valid would start failing, including stored .bowman data validated by IdeaSchema/PhaseSchema; error shapes (describeSchemaError) and z.record/z.enum signatures change. Plan: check every stored id in this repo and fixtures against the strict form first, use z.guid() where loose ids are legitimate, upgrade one package at a time behind pnpm check, run pnpm verify:migration on real projects.

status.comment: zod ^4.6.7 in backend, shared, agent-tools, loop-worker, mcp, real-world and the broker; @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.24 -> ^1.32.2 (accepts zod 3 or 4). Code changes: object defaults `.default({})` -> `.prefault({})` in harness-config (v4 defaults skip parsing), loop roles z.record(enum) -> z.partialRecord (v4 records over an enum are exhaustive), protocol schemas generated with v4's z.toJSONSchema (draft-7, io input) instead of zod-to-json-schema (removed), with additionalProperties:false restored on every object so the published spec stays as strict as before; the only spec change is v4's strict RFC uuid pattern on ids. Checked first: all 925 stored files here have RFC-valid ids; pnpm validate:bowman on this repo: 878 ideas, 10 archived, 37 phases valid. Error wording changed ('cost: Too small: expected number to be >0'); tests updated. Evidence: pnpm check 25/25. pnpm audit --prod: the zod high advisory remains only via voice-bridge's openai@4 SDK (peer zod ^3; optional package, not on the hosted surface; needs an openai major upgrade), plus a moderate uuid in voice-bridge's Google TTS chain.
